headline: ChatGPT is refusing requests to write in famous authors' styles
summary: Ars Technica reports that OpenAI has recently changed its policy, with the chatbot now declining to mimic the styles of both living and dead authors during testing.
details: ChatGPT is now refusing to copy the voices and styles of popular authors, as reported by Ars Technica. Social media posts confirm users are seeing the chatbot decline requests to mimic specific authors' writing.

Ars Technica's testing showed ChatGPT would not comply with prompts to imitate the styles of both living and dead authors. This marks a change, as a previous study by No Latency indicated the chatbot did not refuse such requests for deceased authors.

headline_marked: Dyson V16 Piston Animal [[delivers 315 air-watts]], unseating Gen5Detect as most powerful
headline: Dyson V16 Piston Animal delivers 315 air-watts, unseating Gen5Detect as most powerful
summary: Dyson's new V16 Piston Animal boasts 315 AW, making it their most powerful stick vacuum. However, its high price and mixed performance against older, cheaper models raise questions about its overall value.
details: Dyson's new V16 Piston Animal and its Submarine variant are now the brand's most powerful stick vacuums, boasting 315 air-watts (AW). This marks a significant upgrade from the previous top model, the Gen5Detect, which offered 262 AW.

The V16 introduces the All Floor Cones Sense cleaner head, designed to adapt to both soft and hard floors. It intelligently adjusts suction power and activates a green dust light on hard surfaces, performing well in diverse home environments.

Users can select between Eco, Auto, and Boost modes, controlled via a built-in LCD screen. The V16 is notably the only one of Dyson's three new summer stick vacuums to feature this screen, enhancing user interaction.
Convenience features include two built-in crevice tools and a dust-compactor tool in the bin. A self-emptying docking station is also planned for later this year, though it will be sold separately.

Despite its raw power, testing revealed that the V16's suction capability didn't always outperform Dyson's older lineup. It showed mixed results with sand and cat litter on certain surfaces, sometimes requiring a second pass.

Ultimately, while the V16 Piston Animal is a powerful and capable vacuum, its high price point and comparable performance to the cheaper Gen5Detect suggest it's best for those prioritizing its specific add-on options.
